sections.title: Scientific method
sections.content:
Key terms in scientific investigation:
• hypothesis — a proposed explanation to be tested. The scientist formed a hypothesis about the results.
• empirical — based on observation and experiment. Empirical evidence supports the theory.
• variable — a factor that can change in an experiment. The researchers controlled all variables except temperature.
• correlation — a connection between two things. There is a strong correlation between exercise and mental health.
• peer-reviewed — evaluated by experts before publication. Always cite peer-reviewed sources in academic papers.

sections.title: Discoveries and innovation
sections.content:
Discussing scientific progress:
• groundbreaking — innovative and pioneering. The groundbreaking study changed our understanding of genetics.
• clinical trial — a test of a medical treatment. The drug is currently in clinical trials.
• phenomenon — an observable event. Scientists are studying this unusual phenomenon.
• replicate — reproduce results in another experiment. Other labs were unable to replicate the findings.

exercises.question: A proposed explanation that can be tested is a:
exercises.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation made as a starting point for investigation.

exercises.question: Evidence based on observation rather than theory is:
exercises.explanation: Empirical means based on verifiable observation or experience rather than theory.

exercises.question: Research evaluated by other experts before publication is:
exercises.explanation: Peer-reviewed means evaluated by qualified experts in the same field.

exercises.question: A factor that changes during an experiment is a:
exercises.explanation: A variable is an element that can change or be changed in an experiment.

exercises.question: A connection between two things without proving cause is a:
exercises.hint: They're linked but one may not cause the other.
exercises.explanation: A correlation is a mutual relationship between two things.

exercises.question: To reproduce experimental results is to:
exercises.explanation: To replicate means to reproduce or duplicate the results of an experiment.

exercises.question: An observable event or fact is a:
exercises.explanation: A phenomenon is a fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen.
